originality.rationale: The 2013 full-text Möbius-polynomial work covers the primitive-word cardinality, but not the two-coordinate Fourier moments, complete divisor-indexed normalized Gram eigenvalues, multiplicities or sharp universal frame bound. A 2008 text about aperiodic-pattern counts defines aperiodic as unbordered, a different support and observable; the two read mathematical published-finding corpus notes treat Hamming shells and unit-residue Fourier rows, respectively. Closest published and local claims were compared by implication, not terminology; none of those inspected implies the full result. Older equivalent autocorrelation formulations remain possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent formula for cyclic average power spectra of primitive necklaces, possibly under different terminology, may exist in older symbolic dynamics or coding literature.
The full Duzhin–Pasechnik preprint and other less directly related historical texts were not read; their implications are not conclusively excluded.
No independent external mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Uniform primitive cyclic words are the canonical roots of aperiodic necklaces, used in symbolic dynamics and coding. Their global periodicity constraint destroys coordinate exchangeability but retains an arithmetic cyclic symmetry. The theorem naturally classifies the entire first-coordinate harmonic sampling spectrum, every degeneracy multiplicity, the exact injectivity boundary, and the optimal dimension-free reconstruction bound. The sharp four constant and prime-factor dependence answer stability questions not supplied by necklace counting alone.
